test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Electrician) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A 20 kVA, 2500/250 V, 50 Hz, single-phase transformer gave open circuit test results (on the low voltage side) of 250 V, 1.6 A and 100 W; what is the no-load power factor?
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**No-Load Power Factor of a Transformer**

**Definition:** The no-load power factor of a transformer is the cosine of the angle of lag between the applied voltage and the no-load current. It indicates how effectively the transformer utilizes the current supplied to it when no external load is connected, and only the core losses (magnetizing current and core loss current) are present.

In this problem, the open circuit test results of a single-phase transformer are provided as follows:

 
• Voltage applied during the test (V): 250 V
 
• No-load current (I): 1.6 A
 
• No-load power (P): 100 W
